title: Practice block close
hook: building your own way closes the way King Josiah renewed a covenant: by reading it aloud
tomorrow: why wouldn't a man answer the rabbis who came to his field?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: an invitation. Bread out, the tent flap open, no test at the door. Today the whole practice block closes, with your rule read aloud.

Some promises only count when they're said out loud: a wedding vow, an oath at a citizenship ceremony, even a toast. The book of Kings tells of a scroll found during repairs to the temple in Jerusalem. The high priest tells the king's scribe, in the King James Version: "I have found the book of the law in the house of the LORD." It's read to King Josiah, and when he hears it, he tears his clothes.
screen: `PROMISES SAID OUT LOUD.` → `A SCROLL FOUND IN THE TEMPLE.` → `THE KING TEARS HIS CLOTHES.`

segments.voice: Then he goes further. He gathers priests, prophets and all the people, small and great, and "he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant." He stands by a pillar and binds himself to keep it. And the text adds: "And all the people stood to the covenant." That's a thread in Jewish life: the covenant is renewed by hearing it, together. Deuteronomy commands a public reading of the law before all Israel, and in synagogues the Torah is still read aloud to the gathered people. A text kept in a drawer can be forgotten. A text read aloud is a promise with witnesses, even if the only witness is you. So this block closes Josiah's way. Look back at what built the last stretch. Ready for now, leaves and all. Where I am, a guest and at home. Go and see. Ask them. Tag the source. An invitation, never a push. Your rule isn't scripture. But read aloud, it becomes yours.
screen: `READ IN THE EARS OF ALL.` · `THE PEOPLE STOOD TO THE COVENANT.` · `RENEWED BY HEARING IT.` · `A PROMISE WITH WITNESSES.` · then, large: `READ IT ALOUD; IT BECOMES YOURS.`

segments.voice: Hold the clean copy of your rule and read it aloud once, slowly, in a speaking voice, as if someone you trust were listening. Then sit quietly with the last line still in the air.
Practice block close: the end of building your own way, and your rule, read aloud. Like Josiah's covenant: heard, then kept.
Last line of the block: my rule, read aloud and stood to. Day 1706, and the practice block is closed.

howItsDone: In the synagogue the Torah is read aloud to the congregation, and Deuteronomy 31 commands a public reading of the law before all Israel. On a personal path, a finished rule can be read aloud once, to oneself or to a trusted friend, as a way of taking it on.
